summary: Iteration 34 (Talent Recovery Playbook + Dispute Fee Collection): 20/20 backend tests passing and frontend recovery banner UX verified. Covered: recovery-status endpoint (clean/penalised/employer 403), under_review lifts after 3 clean approvals, excessive_revisions lifts after 5 (with visibility_score->100 and rate_bias_pct->0), rejection resets streak, dirty (revision_count>0) approvals do NOT increment streak, approve regression on submitted+revision_resubmitted, dispute -> admin ruling notification + deliverable stamping (dispute_grievance_id / dispute_ref / dispute_opened_at) + status transition to dispute_resolved, POST /grievances/{id}/pay-fee (real Stripe test-mode session created with metadata.kind='dispute_fee' & payer_id, amount=$49), 403 for winner/admin/unrelated, 400 for unresolved, 404 for missing, GET /grievances/{id}/fee-status permissions, and Stripe webhook (signed HMAC) marking payment_status=paid idempotently. Frontend Talent Dashboard renders [data-testid=recovery-banner] with '2 more clean approvals' and progress bar width=33% for streak=1/under_review, and hides for a clean talent.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2880+ lines — split into modules (deliverables, engagements, stripe) for maintainability.

pay-fee: if a session was created earlier and Stripe returns status='expired', the code falls through and creates a new session but does not clean up the old dispute_fee_transactions row (leaves stale 'initiated' rows). Consider marking it 'expired'.

mark_dispute_fee_paid queries by session_id only; if the same session_id somehow points at a different grievance the payer_id / grievance_id mismatch is not validated. Low risk since Stripe session ids are unique, but a metadata cross-check would be defensive.
admin_rule_dispute email send is best-effort (try/except pass) which is correct; consider logging.warning so failures are still observable.
